decision_reason: Iteration 1 returned strong broad coverage — Brazilian MoH bulletins (gov.br), PAHO situation reports (paho.org), state-level sources (saude.mg.gov.br, saude.df.gov.br, goias.gov.br, cevs.rs.gov.br), InfoDengue (info.dengue.mat.br), and open data (dadosabertos.saude.gov.br) are all represented. However, several critical gaps remain for the specific Q1 2024 (SE 1–13) window: (1) The most directly relevant MoH bulletin found (gov.br, SE 4 snippet) covers only through SE 4; we need the dedicated Q1 2024 dengue bulletin (Boletim Epidemiológico Especial or the COE-Dengue weekly reports for SE 1–13). (2) The PAHO results found are dated June 2024 and October 2024 — no Q1-specific PAHO alert or situation report covering Jan–Mar 2024 has been confirmed. (3) The Minas Gerais and Distrito Federal state bulletins found appear to cover later periods (SE 52/2024, June 2024); Q1-specific state-level data for the highest-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás) is not yet confirmed. (4) The COE-Dengue emergency declaration (February 2024) and associated quantitative thresholds have not been surfaced. (5) ProMED/WHO Disease Outbreak News entries for the Q1 2024 Brazil dengue emergency have not appeared. A second iteration with 4 targeted queries can close these gaps within the allowed budget (10 total queries, 2 iterations max).
coverage_assessment: Broad source-type coverage is good: official Brazilian MoH (gov.br), PAHO (paho.org), state health secretariats (MG, DF, GO, RS), InfoDengue/SINAN (info.dengue.mat.br, dadosabertos.saude.gov.br), and international news (NPR, NYT) are all represented. However, temporal precision for Q1 2024 (SE 1–13, Jan–Mar) is weak: the MoH bulletin snippet covers only through SE 4; PAHO results are mid-year or later; state bulletins appear to cover later periods. The COE-Dengue emergency declaration (Feb 2024) and its quantitative case/death thresholds — a high-value evidence item — have not been confirmed in any result. The dedicated PAHO Q1 2024 epidemiological alert for Brazil dengue is also absent.
source_diversity_assessment: Good diversity across source types (official agency, international org, structured database, news, academic). State-level diversity is partial: MG, DF, GO, RS appear but São Paulo (highest burden state in Q1 2024) and Rio de Janeiro are not yet confirmed. The InfoDengue (info.dengue.mat.br) and dadosabertos.saude.gov.br domains appeared, which is positive for structured data, but no Q1-specific data has been confirmed from these. Wikipedia and YouTube results are low-value and should not be used as primary sources.
trustworthiness_assessment: High-trust sources are present: gov.br (MoH/SVSA), paho.org, saude.mg.gov.br, saude.df.gov.br, goias.gov.br, cevs.rs.gov.br, dadosabertos.saude.gov.br, info.dengue.mat.br. Medium-trust: apm.org.br (medical association, cites MoH), reliefweb.int (OCHA aggregator of PAHO content), NPR, NYT. Low-trust or out-of-scope: ecologiaesaude.com (secondary aggregator), youtube.com, en.wikipedia.org, beaconbio.org, firstwordpharma.com — these should not be used as primary evidence sources. The gov.br PDF (SE 4 bulletin) is the highest-value result found so far.
disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: strong (all results are dengue-specific). Location fit: strong (Brazil national and subnational). Time fit: WEAK for Q1 2024 specifically. The MoH bulletin found covers SE 4 (late January 2024) — this is within scope but only covers the first month. The PAHO and APM results cover SE 1–26 (full first half of 2024), which includes Q1 but is not Q1-specific. State bulletins found appear to cover later periods. The COE-Dengue emergency (declared ~Feb 2024) and the dedicated Q1 dengue bulletin are the key missing time-specific items.
corroboration_potential_assessment: The gov.br MoH bulletin (SE 4, >260k probable cases) and the APM summary (6.2M notifications SE 1–26) provide national-level figures but at different temporal scopes. PAHO June 2024 update corroborates the record-breaking scale but does not isolate Q1. State-level corroboration is partial. A Q1-specific COE-Dengue bulletin or the dedicated Boletim Epidemiológico Especial Dengue 2024 (typically published by SVSA around SE 13–15) would provide the most precise Q1 case/death totals and enable cross-validation with PAHO Q1 figures. ProMED posts from Jan–Mar 2024 would provide independently timestamped corroboration.

The PAHO March 28, 2024 press release is squarely within Q1 2024. The COE-Dengue SE 01–05 and SE 01–11 informes cover January–March 2024 (SE 1 ≈ Jan 1, SE 13 ≈ Mar 30).
